title: kdash per-host update issue
description: Payload of kdash:update:{host}:{kind} — latest-value, presence-owned, no TTL, exactly 4 segments. One statement that the update run on {host} needs Ken, of one kind. {host} is the host's inventory name; {kind} names the issue (`ring-stopped`, `reboot-awaiting`, `held`, `gate-failed` today — an OPEN vocabulary: a reader renders an unknown kind by its `issue` line rather than dropping it). Both segments use rules.md's host-token grammar and both are authoritative; the payload echoes neither. One key per (host, kind) so two issues on one host — a held package and a pending reboot — coexist and clear independently. CD-18 applies verbatim, as for kdash:stale: (1) THE KEY'S PRESENCE IS THE FLAG — SET when the issue arises, DELeted when it is resolved, and absence is the only all-clear; no TTL and no staleness window. (2) A MALFORMED PAYLOAD MUST NOT CLEAR THE FLAG: a reader that cannot parse it still shows the host as needing attention, with the detail missing.

since.description: Unix seconds (float) of when this issue was FIRST raised on this host. Set once and carried unchanged across every later run that finds the same issue still standing (read-modify-write with `kdash-pub get`); a writer that restamps it turns 'held for three weeks' into 'held since this morning'.

ts.description: Unix seconds (float) of the LAST write — the most recent run that found this issue still standing. Moves every run; `since` does not.

issue.description: The one short human line the card renders, e.g. 'rpi53: reboot needed for linux-image 6.12.48'. Rendered verbatim, so it carries the whole explanation; minLength because an empty line is a red row nobody can act on, maxLength because it is one line on a panel, not a log.

ref.description: Optional korg node the issue is tracked under (`korg:<id>`), so a reader can name where to look. Absent when nothing has been filed.

examples.issue: rpi53: reboot needed for linux-image 6.12.48 (apt run 2026-11-02)
kai: apt ring stopped — gate failed on kubs0

x-counterexamples.why: the issue line is what the card renders; an empty one is a flag with no explanation
k-homelab's other timestamps are ISO 8601 strings, and this is the slip WI 1926 was filed for: it publishes cleanly and surfaces as a blank card two repos away
`since` is the stamp the read-modify-write must carry; dropping it makes every run look like the first

record.issue: rpi53: reboot needed for linux-image 6.12.48 (apt run 2026-11-02)

x-counterexamples.why: `ref` is a korg locator, `korg:<id>`; a bare number reads as a work item, a proposal or nothing depending on who reads it

record.issue: rpi53: reboot needed for linux-image 6.12.48 (apt run 2026-11-02)

x-counterexamples.why: a millisecond stamp would read as permanently fresh; every new family's `ts` is bounded at 1e11
